text:
# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

name: INSIGHTS.md
text:
# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## MEASUREMENT RESOLUTION on this run (read this before believing any small win)
- What worked (confirmed by a RESULT): nothing yet moved val beyond noise. Round 1's decisive
  number is not a candidate delta at all: two BYTE-IDENTICAL null-control replicates of the seed
  (ctl_null_i0, ctl_null_i0r1 — same bytes, same seeds, same n_trials=3, full 10-task val) scored
  **0.6000 and 0.4667**, so `null_delta_between_control_replicates = 0.1333`. The stored baseline
  (0.50) vs a fresh control also drifted 0.10 (`parent_vs_gate_ref_drift`). This run's evidence bar
  is therefore ~0.13 reward on full val at 3 trials.
- Consequence for future iterations: a candidate must move val by MORE than roughly one whole task
  (0.1 = one of ten tasks flipping all three trials) before the gate can see it. Chasing two or three
  single-trial fixes in one round is not enough — the round must credibly flip a WHOLE task, or
  several. Do not present a delta of 0.05–0.10 as a win; the gate will not, and neither should the
  report.

## Cluster: formula text read as a number (`data_only=True`)
- What worked: the FIX itself is verified at the code level, independent of the gate — replaying
  374-9's own final solution code with `data_only=True` added and nothing else changed makes all 32
  graded cells match gold including the float type at B10 (0/3 -> 3/3). This is the only edit in the
  run so far with an end-to-end verification.
- What didn't (confirmed by RESULT): shipping that fact as PROSE did not reliably produce the fix.
  cand_1a (prompt.md, full knowledge sections, 948 words) came out at reward 0.5111, gate_delta
  −0.0889, and REGRESSED 52216 and 53161 — the one candidate in the round with a stable verdict, and
  it was a reject. Knowledge stated in the system prompt is not knowledge applied.
- Promising but not yet tried: make the typed read OBSERVABLE rather than advised. The strongest
  form available on the two editable surfaces is a worked code block the agent can copy in round 1
  (cand_1b does this and was the round's best at 0.60) — but going further, the template could
  require the agent to print `type(...).__name__` for the exact source cells and quote those types
  back before it is allowed to compute.

## Form matters more than content on this reader (gemma-4-31B-it)
- What didn't: the largest prose addition (cand_1a, prompt.md only) scored WORST of the three and
  regressed two previously-passing tasks. More rules on the system-prompt surface traded correct
  behaviour for rule-following.
- What worked best, though not resolvably: the STRUCTURAL edit on `task_template.md` (cand_1b) —
  turning the 3-round list into an ordered procedure whose round 3 is check-by-comparison, and
  DELETING the old "reply without a code block when you are satisfied" + "print the values you
  wrote" lines. reward 0.6000 vs the run's 0.50 baseline, gate_delta ≈ 0.0 against a fresh control,
  no regressions on any task. Inside the 0.1333 noise floor, so inconclusive, not an accept.
- Promising but not yet tried: the composition (cand_1c, both surfaces, 0.5556) landed BETWEEN its
  two parents, which is the signature of the prose surface actively costing something. If a future
  round wants both, put the knowledge INSIDE the procedure step that needs it rather than in
  prompt.md.

## Rules that look obviously right and are NOT (do not re-derive these)
Verified against the fixtures and the adapter, not guessed. Half this suite is row-deletion /
row-shift work, so each of these regresses a currently-passing task:
- "Always edit in place with openpyxl, never rebuild with `df.to_excel`" — 160-6's PASSING mechanism
  is `dropna(how='all')` + `to_excel`; the row shift IS the answer. Also hits 47484 and 418-29.
  8 of 12 passing traces.
- "Leave every cell outside answer_position identical; never blank a cell inside it" — factually
  false here: 160-6's gold changes 30 cells OUTSIDE answer_position, 418-29's gold blanks 4 INSIDE
  it, 347-49's gold blanks 237. The adapter grades ONLY cells inside answer_position, so the
  outside-range half is not even a contract the scorer holds.
- "Diff input vs output and fix outside-range differences" — would order 160-6 to undo its correct
  row shift, turning 3/3 into ~0.

## Still-uncracked clusters, with what is known about each
- **347-49 (0/3, the largest single gap):** its blank-run scan uses `else: break`, stopping at the
  first non-blank row, so it deletes 10 rows where gold deletes 72 (a repeating header block).
  Verified to reproduce the scorer's 1037/222/182/92 counts exactly. A pure pandas round-trip with
  NO deletion is byte-identical to the input, so `to_excel` is not the culprit — the scan logic is.
- **32468 (0/3):** t0/t1 use a 12-month window where gold implies 13; the instruction names a ~39M
  anchor no trial ever checked. t2 separately pairs `range(4,35)` (pandas, header consumed) with
  `row = 5 + idx` (openpyxl) and lands every value one month late plus a trailing `None` at I35.
- **55457 (0/3):** its `instruction` field is literally blank, so the value semantics are
  UNKNOWABLE from the prompt. Only its filler damage is addressable, and trial t1 already shows the
  A/B: dropping `else: results.append(0)` removed all 5 filler violations at no cost.
- **53161 (0.333):** t0 is a one-column extent error (`range(6,31)` = F..AD, missing AE); t2
  hardcodes table rows 16/17/21 when the real block is header 11, data 12–17.
- **40467 (0.667):** t2 only — `read_excel(p)` paired with `to_excel(header=False)`, one-row shift.

name: JOURNAL.md
text:
# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_1a / cand_1b / cand_1c (round 1) — fix the silent formula-string read + the print-is-not-a-check verification, on two different surfaces

- Changes I made (per sibling; all three target the SAME diagnosed clusters, deliberately on DIFFERENT surfaces/forms):
  - cand_1a — `prompt.md` ONLY. Four added sections, all KNOWLEDGE / worked-example form: (1) `load_workbook()` without
    `data_only=True` returns formula TEXT, so an `isinstance(v,(int,float))` guard silently drops it and totals come out
    too LOW — with a worked two-handle read/write example [cluster: "number LOWER than expected", 374-9 x3, 53161 t2];
    (2) never pad a range with invented `0`/`''`/`None`, WITH an explicit carve-out that instruction-directed blanking
    and row-shift blanks ARE the answer [55457 t0/t2, 32468 t2]; (3) the DataFrame-index vs Excel-row offset table
    (+2 / +1 / none) and the read/write header-pairing rule [40467 t2, 32468 t2]; (4) derive extents from the data, and
    Python's exclusive upper bound [53161 t0, 347-49].
  - cand_1b — `task_template.md` ONLY. Same clusters, STRUCTURAL form instead of knowledge: the 3-step round list is
    rewritten as an ORDERED procedure in which each step is a precondition of the next; round 1 is a look-before-compute
    round that must print source cells WITH their types; round 3 becomes "check by COMPARISON" (recompute one target
    cell by a second route, cell count vs the TARGET SIZE the adapter already prints, row count before/after, any total
    the instruction itself names). DELETED the old line "Reply without a code block when you are satisfied the saved
    file is correct" and the old round-3 wording "re-open output_path and print the values you wrote" — the traces show
    that print-only step is exactly what let every failure through.
  - cand_1c — BOTH surfaces, composed without duplication: 1a's knowledge in `prompt.md`, plus a shorter ordered
    procedure in `task_template.md` that INVOKES the checks rather than restating the facts.
- Expected effect + why safe: the formula-read fix is the one edit verified end-to-end — replaying 374-9's own final
  code with `data_only=True` added and nothing else changed makes all 32 cells match gold, including the float type on
  B10 (0/3 -> 3/3). Blast radius checked against all 12 passing traces: 52216 t1/t2 already pass `data_only=True`;
  47484 / 160-6 / 418-29 read via pandas (already cached values), so the rule is a no-op for them; adding the flag to
  52216 t0's read was verified to produce byte-identical output. Every kept edit is ADDITIVE, or a clarification of a
  contract the passing tasks already satisfy.
- What I deliberately did NOT ship, having diagnosed it as UNSAFE (the round's main finding): three rules that read as
  obvious fixes each regress a currently-passing task, because half this suite is row-deletion/shift work rather than
  fill-a-column work. (i) "always edit in place with openpyxl, never rebuild via df.to_excel" would force 160-6 off the
  `dropna` + `to_excel` rewrite that IS its passing mechanism, and 47484 / 418-29 t0/t1 too — 8 of 12 passing traces.
  (ii) "leave every cell outside answer_position identical / never blank a cell inside it" is FALSE here: 160-6's own
  gold changes 30 cells OUTSIDE answer_position, 418-29's gold blanks 4 cells INSIDE it, and 347-49's gold blanks 237.
  (iii) "diff input vs output and fix any outside-range difference" would order 160-6 to undo its correct row shift.
  Confirmed from the adapter: grading reads ONLY cells inside answer_position, so an outside-range diff is not a
  contract the scorer holds the agent to. I scoped edit (2) with an explicit carve-out instead of shipping (ii).
- Building on prior RESULTS: none exist — this is round 1 (LEDGER holds the baseline only; rejected.jsonl absent).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet by a RESULT. The three rules above are recorded as diagnosed-unsafe-before-spending,
  which is not the same as refuted by measurement.
- High-value clusters still not cracked: 32468 (12- vs 13-month window — a semantic guess; the instruction names a ~39M
  anchor that no trial ever checked, which the round-3 comparison step only reaches indirectly) and 55457 (its
  `instruction` field is literally blank, so the value semantics are unknowable; only its filler and type damage is
  addressable). 347-49 needs its blank-run scan to span a repeating HEADER block, addressed here only via the row-count
  check.
- Focus next round: read whichever sibling gates best and check in its traces whether round 1 / round 3 were actually
  EXERCISED. Never exercised => the FORM is wrong (switch surface); exercised and still wrong => the content is.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.511 Δ=+0.011 · fixed={—} · broke={52216} · unresolved={40467, 53161} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
<!-- cand_1a: rejected val=0.511 Δ=+0.011 -->

## Iteration cand_1c — (duplicate handover; optimizer re-appended a prior entry unchanged)

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** UNRESOLVED (not judged; champion unchanged) · val=0.556 Δ=— · fixed={—} · broke={—} · unresolved={40467, 52216} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — the measurement could not separate this edit from re-measurement noise, so it is NOT evidence against the edit. Its batch was still reverted. To resolve it, re-measure it under a FRESH tag (re-running the same tag REPLACES its rollouts) or with more trials in ONE evaluation; do not redesign it on this round's numbers, and do not re-derive it as a new idea.
<!-- cand_1c: unresolved val=0.556 Δ=— -->

name: LEDGER.md
text:
# LEDGER — factual run record (framework-maintained; READ-ONLY)

The measured record of every iteration: which candidate, its parent, whether the gate ACCEPTED it, the val reward + Δ, and the tasks it broke / fixed. Facts only — your own narrative, lessons, and refuted hypotheses go in JOURNAL.md. Use this to never re-introduce a change that broke a task, and to see which approaches the gate accepted vs rejected.

`broke` / `fixed` list only tasks whose move EXCEEDED 2·SE of its own per-task measurement error, so they are claims the measurement can support. A task that moved by less is in `unresolved`: it is NOT evidence the edit did anything to that task, in either direction, and must not be reasoned about as a regression or a win. Do not redesign an edit because a task appears there — re-measure it, or ignore it.

## Iterations
| iter | candidate | parent | outcome | val | Δ vs parent | broke (were passing) | fixed | unresolved (moved < 2·SE) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | cand_1a | seed | reject | 0.511 | +0.011 | {52216} | {} | {40467, 53161} |
| 2 | cand_1c | seed | reject | 0.556 |  | {} | {} | {40467, 52216} |

name: META_INSIGHTS.md
text:
# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Round 1 (cand_1a / cand_1b / cand_1c)
- **Strategy tried:** diagnose first with read-only subagents and spend ZERO rollouts on diagnosis,
  then field 3 siblings that attack the SAME diagnosed clusters on DIFFERENT surfaces/forms
  (knowledge-on-prompt.md vs structure-on-task_template.md vs both), so the round learns which FORM
  the reader responds to even if no sibling gates. That part worked: the form signal is clean and
  monotone (1b 0.600 > 1c 0.556 > 1a 0.511), and it is the single most useful thing this round
  produced. The diagnosis itself was strong — one cluster (`data_only=True` on 374-9) was verified
  end-to-end by replaying the agent's own code against the real fixture, no rollout needed.
- **Did it move val?** No, not resolvably. LEDGER: cand_1b inconclusive (0.600, gate_delta ≈ 0.0,
  verdict_stable false, no regressions), cand_1c inconclusive (0.556, −0.044, verdict_stable false),
  cand_1a reject (0.511, −0.089, verdict_stable TRUE, regressions 52216 + 53161).
- **The stall signal is not the candidates — it is the instrument.** Two byte-identical control
  replicates of the SEED differed by 0.1333 (0.600 vs 0.467), and the stored baseline vs a fresh
  control drifted 0.10. On a 10-task val at 3 trials one task = 0.1 reward, so the noise floor is
  wider than a whole task. Two of three siblings came back `verdict_stable: false` for exactly this
  reason: they accept against one control replicate and reject against the other. That is the
  binding constraint on this run, and no amount of better prose fixes it.
- **Lever this implies (and the accounting that blocks it):** the right move after a round like this
  is to buy TRIALS on the best sibling rather than field a fourth guess — resolution, not novelty.
  `grow.py` is the intended instrument, but it only returns `grow_again` when `d.delta > 0`, and the
  two inconclusive siblings sit at 0.0 and −0.044, so its own logic returns `abandon`. Growth
  genuinely cannot help them, which is the documented condition for booking
  `commit.py --decision inconclusive --force`. With `max_iterations = 3` and one iteration charged
  per commit, the three gated siblings ARE the whole budget: there is no round 2 to spend the lever
  on. Recording this so a future run sees the trap, not to excuse it.
- **What to try next iteration (or next run):** (1) Fix the instrument before the capability — on a
  10-task split, budget for more trials per candidate (5–7) or accept that only whole-task flips are
  visible, and size each round to flip a WHOLE task rather than to shave several single trials.
  (2) Go after 347-49 and 32468, the two 0/3 tasks: together they are 0.2 of val, comfortably above
  the noise floor, whereas the 53161/40467 single-trial slips (0.033 each) are invisible by
  construction. (3) Prefer the `task_template.md` structural surface over `prompt.md` prose for this
  reader tier; the round's one stable verdict was the prose-only candidate being REJECTED with
  regressions, while the structural one was the round's best and regressed nothing.
- **Process note on the harness:** `round.py` refused a direct full-val gate until `--skip-screen-
  ladder` was passed. Skipping was correct here (on a 10-task val the tier-1 floor puts the screen's
  break-even kill rate out of reach), but a future run on a small split should expect that prompt
  and budget the argument up front rather than losing a cycle to it.

<!-- cap-evolve:meta-insights-append-below -->

name: prompt.md
text:
You are a spreadsheet expert who can manipulate spreadsheets through Python code.

Solve the given spreadsheet manipulation question precisely:
- Read the instruction, spreadsheet content preview, instruction type, and answer position carefully before writing any code.
- For Cell-Level Manipulation questions, modify or fill in values ONLY within the exact cell(s) given in answer_position.
- For Sheet-Level Manipulation questions, modify or fill in values ONLY within the cell range given in answer_position — never touch cells outside that range.
- Prefer computing and writing LITERAL values (e.g. with pandas/openpyxl) over live spreadsheet formulas, so the result is unambiguous when the file is re-opened for grading.
- Always save your result to the exact output_path given, creating any missing parent directories first.
- If code execution returns an error, read the traceback carefully and fix the code — do not repeat a failing approach unchanged.

name: task_template.md
text:
<!--
  THE AGENT'S JOB DESCRIPTION — editable capability text, same as prompt.md.

  Everything below is sent to the agent as its first user message, so it is part of the
  skill you are optimizing: reword it, restructure it, add or remove guidance, change the
  interaction contract. This comment block is STRIPPED before the agent sees it.

  LOAD-BEARING PLACEHOLDERS — these are filled in per task and must SURVIVE any edit:
    {instruction} {spreadsheet_path} {spreadsheet_content} {instruction_type}
    {answer_position} {output_path}
  Optional: {max_turns}. No other {braces} are allowed.

  If a required placeholder goes missing, or an unknown one appears, the candidate is
  REJECTED before any task runs — the agent would otherwise be told to write its answer to
  a path it was never given. A literal brace must be doubled: {{ or }}.
-->
You need to solve the following spreadsheet manipulation question. It contains six pieces of information:
- instruction: the question about spreadsheet manipulation.
- spreadsheet_path: the path of the spreadsheet file you need to manipulate.
- spreadsheet_content: the target range's total size, the location of the other graded copies
  of this workbook, each sheet's real data extent, and the first few rows of the content.
- instruction_type: Cell-Level Manipulation (answer_position is exact cell(s)) or Sheet-Level Manipulation (answer_position is the maximum range you may modify).
- answer_position: the cell(s)/range you must modify or fill in.
- output_path: write the modified spreadsheet file to this exact path.

### instruction
{instruction}

### spreadsheet_path
{spreadsheet_path}

### spreadsheet_content
{spreadsheet_content}

### instruction_type
{instruction_type}

### answer_position
{answer_position}

### output_path
{output_path}

You have up to {max_turns} rounds of interaction. In each round, reply with exactly ONE python code block:
1. Information-gathering code (e.g. inspecting the file) — the execution result is returned to you.
2. Solution code that writes the modified file to output_path.
3. Verification code: re-open output_path and print the values you wrote in answer_position,
   to confirm they are correct before finishing. If they are wrong, fix your code and write again.
Reply without a code block when you are satisfied the saved file is correct.
If your code raises an error, the traceback will be returned to you; fix the code and try again.
